text:
Samir Patel: Quick heads-up — JadeView dedicated bring-up dry run tomorrow 09:30 PT. Goal: validate quota, autoscale triggers, and fallback. Can we confirm who's on-watch and any outstanding blockers?
Iris Chen: I'll be on infra watch. Need confirmation on reserved pool size + KMS access for customer logs.
Anya Dorsey: On enablement — I have the customer runbook and can steer their engineers. Do they have the CLI creds?
Mike R: CS noted they need quota increase for embeddings path. Samir, did we already submit the request?
Samir Patel: Submitted ticket #INC-8271 last night for quota bump to 10 reserved GPUs; pending approvals from capacity team. Iris, can you confirm the pool name we will use?
Iris Chen: Pool is jadeview-prod-reserved. Current provisioned GPUs = 6. If quota bump clears, autoscaler target_max = 12.
Anya Dorsey: I pushed the onboarding checklist to JadeView team — they said they can run smoke tests but want a short guide for the k6 script. I'll paste the snippet here for them.
Anya Dorsey: ```bash
# k6 smoke script example
k6 run --vus 100 --duration 5m load/jadeview_smoke.js 
  -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$JADEVIEW_API_KEY 
  -e MODEL=redwood-embed-2-small
```
Mike R: For autoscale, let's validate both capacity-based and latency-based triggers. Suggest: scale_out when 95th_p50_token_latency > 300ms OR GPU_util > 75% for 3m.
Iris Chen: Agreed. Current autoscale policy draft: 
```yaml
policy_name: jadeview-autoscale-dryrun
metrics:
  - name: gpu_util
    threshold: 75
    duration: 180s
  - name: token_p50_latency_ms
    threshold: 300
    duration: 180s
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 12
cooldown: 300s
```
Samir Patel: Good. Also ensure prefix KV caching enabled for 1h; customer uses many repeated prompts. Saves costs during stress test.
Iris Chen: KV caching flag is on for jadeview-prod-reserved. I'm going to run a short probe now to confirm metrics pipeline.
deploy-bot: [09:15] autoscaler-check: metrics pipeline OK, alerting hooks healthy, canary route registered for jadeview-prod-reserved.
Iris Chen: Running k6 locally against staging endpoint to produce traffic profile (100->400 VUs ramp). Will post logs.
Mike R: Reminder: have fallback model variant ready (redwood-lite-quant) if memory pressure trips. Team should verify graceful fallback and error codes.
Anya Dorsey: Adding a short steps section for JadeView engineers: 1) validate API key 2) run k6 smoke 3) watch telemetry dashboard tab 'jadeview-dryrun' 4) confirm A/B model fallback works.
Samir Patel: Can someone confirm KMS access? Customer needs to write logs to their KMS.
Iris Chen: KMS policies are attached to the VPC connector for jadeview. I verified 'putObject' and 'encrypt' permissions.
deploy-bot: [09:22] quota-ticket INC-8271 status: awaiting-capacity-approval. Estimated approval: 2h.
Mike R: If quota approval is delayed, plan B is to shadow traffic across two smaller pools and adjust routing policy to region priority. Samir, we documented failover routes in the runbook.
Samir Patel: Yep — routing policy 'jadeview-fallback' exists and will split 30% -> regional-shard if pool hits soft-cap.
Anya Dorsey: I'll run the customer enablement call at 09:10 to walk them through observability: token-level cost, latency per route, and how to trigger a rollback.
Iris Chen: One more note — during the last dryrun we saw a Kv-cache warmup lag of ~90s; tweak suggestion: pre-warm with a 5-min warm traffic window.
Samir Patel: Good catch. Add pre-warm window 5m before ramp to the checklist.
Mike R: I'll prepare the load profile and share the script to S3: s3://rwinf-test/jadeview/dryrun/2026-03-24.
Anya Dorsey: Customer confirmation: @jadeview-eng replied 'ready for 09:30, will join enablement call'.
Samir Patel: OK — final ask: reactions if you're committed to watch the dry run at 09:30.
Iris Chen: :thumbsup:
Anya Dorsey: :thumbsup:
Mike R: :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: Thanks everyone — will post post-mortem thread after the run.
